To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of oxaliplatin in N-RCT for ESCC is associated with a significantly lower rate of complete resection and lower survival than the use of cisplatin.
oxaliplatin based N-RCT resulted with a poorer outcome in patients with ESCC.
the use of oxaliplatin instead of cisplatin for N-RCT of esophageal cancer is associated with a higher risk for incomplete resection and poorer outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of the quantum Hall effect in the presence of a magnetic field.
the development of an effective, safe and well-tolerated radiochemotherapy (RCT) regimen for the treatment of esophageal cancer (EC).
a comparison of the results of two different N-RCT regimens in the treatment of ESCC patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of oxaliplatin in the neoadjuvant setting in ESCC is not recommended and should only be considered in clinical studies.
the combination of oxaliplatin and radiotherapy is a safe regimen and should be further investigated in phase II studies.
the oxaliplati-based regimen is not superior to the cisplatin/5-FU-based regimen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cisplatin based regimen is better than the oxaliplatiin regimen for esophageal cancer patients.
the use of oxaliplatin in N-RCT for ESCC is not recommended, and cisplatin remains the gold standard.
the use of oxaliplatin in N-RCT is associated with a higher rate of R0 resection and lower rates of pathological complete response, compared with cisplatin-based treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cisplatin-based regimens should remain the standard of care for N-RCT for esophageal SCC.
oxaliplatin is a poor replacement for cisplatin in N-RCT for ESCC, and that cisplatin should remain the standard of care for this indication.
oxaliplatin should not be routinely used in place of cisplatin in N-RCT for ESCC.
